Per registers.yaml's own caveat it is "not found used by this method": a #define with no reference is what an unused constant looks like, and it is not proof the byte is unused on the hardware. FLIPS AGAINST THE ISSUE'S OWN LIST, on dated evidence. registers.yaml's 0x0743 entry records a live test against nvidia-smi on 2026-09-23 (evidence/ec-watch/2026-09-23-ctgp-live.txt): setting 0x0743 bit 2 with 0x0744 raised the enforced limit 120 -> 130 W and clearing it restored 120, which is exactly upstream's ctgp_offset path (write 0x0744, enable 0x0743). docs/findings.md "Feature-by-feature driver verification" still lists this as untested; that summary predates the 2026-09-23 note and the note is the later evidence. Claimed WITH the taper caveat, not a cap. 0x07A6 is confirmed-working-partially: the profile write changes the early-exit taper and does not cap charging (ec/annotations/charge-target-derating.md; docs/findings.md "Charge threshold"). evidence/battery-traces/2026-09-09-profiles.csv has charging rows at capacity >= 95 under Trickle and Long_Life, so >1 A still flows at 95% under both.

0x07B9 is unknown-not-absent, NOT absent, and this repository does not restate the difference away. The paired 0x07B9/0x07D0 write was run live in five variants and charging never stopped; both candidate writers are private with no caller; what exists is a 16.4 V charge-voltage target the EC owns and the host cannot set (docs/findings.md "Charge threshold", sections 4a-4o). The driver would expose a threshold this board does not honour.

Wrong mechanism rather than a hardware fault: 0x0748-0x074B were written live with the animation running and every write landed, changed nothing, and there is no site in either image (docs/findings.md "The lightbar"). The chassis lightbar is 048D:6005 on its own HID ID, so it belongs in ite_8291_lb (issue #5), not in this driver.

Refuted live, not merely unclaimed: Fn+F5 emits no WMI event at all (docs/findings.md "Feature-by-feature driver verification"). Upstream implements this as TOUCHPAD_TOGGLE_OFF bit 6 of EC_ADDR_OEM_4 at 0x07A6, so an address IS readable for it -- the exclusion is the live result, and would stand even with the address known.

The EC bit flips on write and the real-world effect is untested (docs/findings.md "Feature-by-feature driver verification"). An accepted write is not working behaviour: a register the EC reads back correctly is evidence the byte is writable, not that the EC acts on it. Upstream drives TRIGGER_USB_CHARGING bit 4 of EC_ADDR_TRIGGER at 0x0767, so the address is readable here too.

0x0726 is carried at absent, and that is the whole of the claim: a static zero is not proof. Per registers.yaml's own caveat an absent grade rests on a scan finding zero direct references, which is "not found by this method" and never "does not exist"; 0x07B0-0x07BE is a known blind spot of that same scan. The entry's own note says the real verdict is unknown and needs a live behavioural test. Upstream uses AC_AUTO_BOOT_ENABLE bit 3 of EC_ADDR_OEM_9 at 0x0726.

0x07CC is unknown-not-absent: the six reference sites that made it look present are all in the ITE8850-PD image, not the EC firmware, and per registers.yaml that is not "absent" either. This is exactly the case that earned unknown-not-absent its place in the vocabulary.

The kbd_led_* values are left at upstream's default rather than a plausible value being invented; whether this board needs one at all is a hardware question for a human.
